stories.text: Thomas Humber started making bicycles in Nottingham, and around 1878 moved the business to Beeston, where a new works was built for it. The firm later had works in Coventry and Wolverhampton too.

49084.sum: Humber Works is an industrial building.

aka: Building D6 at Boots Factory Site
52289.cat: Building D6 at Boots Beeston Factory Site

stories.text: In 1935–38 Owen Williams built a second factory for Boots, for tablets and lozenges, which gave it its nickname, the "Drys". It too is listed Grade I.

52289.sum: Boots D6 building, on Main Road. Today it houses Medicity. The building dates from about 1936, according to Historic England (via Wikipedia). It is Grade I listed as Building D6 at Boots Factory Site.

52291.cat: Building D10 At Boots Factory Site

stories.text: In 1930–32 the engineer Owen Williams built this factory for Boots' liquid medicines, which gave it its nickname, the "Wets". It is listed Grade I, the largest Grade I-listed structure in Britain.

52291.sum: Building D10 is an industrial building on Main Road. The building was built in 1932, according to OpenStreetMap. It is Grade I listed and was designed by Owen Williams.
